newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND CALL UP TEENAGE VETTORI FOR TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND CALL UP TEENAGE VETTORI FOR TEST.

text.p: New Zealand on Saturday called up teenage spinner Daniel Vettori with just two first class games to face England in the second test starting in Wellington next week.
The 18-year-old is one of three changes made to the New Zealand 12 which earlier this week scrambled a desperate draw in the first of the three-match series.

Senior new ball bowler Danny Morrison has been dumped in favour of in-form left-armer Geoff Allott while middle-order batsman and part-time leg spinner Chris Harris replaces allrounder Justin Vaughan.
But it is the Vettori selection which has provided one of the biggest shocks in recent New Zealand cricket history.
Vettori, who will become New Zealand's youngest test debutant at 18 years 10 days if he plays next week, was ready for the challenge, chairman of selectors Ross Dykes said.
"I think every now and then you get somebody special like this and if the head's right, age is only a number."
Dykes said Vettori's ability to turn and flight the ball gave him outstanding potential.
"He's developed so quickly that he's at the head of the left-arm slows now. He keeps reaffirming what we think of him."

Vettori, who finished high school at the end of 1996, made his first-class debut against England for Northern Districts earlier in their tour, taking a tidy one for 30 off 20 overs, then picked up eight wickets against Central Districts earlier this week.
The lack of penetration among New Zealand's fast-medium bowlers in the drawn first test at Auckland was a key factor in Morrison losing out to the lively Allott.
"In the first test we lacked firepower," Dykes said.
Lee Germon (captain), Bryan Young, Blair Pocock, Adam Parore, Stephen Fleming, Nathan Astle, Chris Cairns, Chris Harris, Dipak Patel, Simon Doull, Geoff Allott, Daniel Vettori.
